Empirical Research Plan ‑ “Credit-Market Concentration, Local Real Activity, and Crime”

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Preferred design: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed-effects) with an event-study extension.  
Why appropriate:  

• Sharp, well–timed shocks to local banking competition were generated by large bank-merger consummations.  
• Which neighborhoods are affected is predetermined by the branch map that existed prior to the merger; this delivers plausibly exogenous cross-sectional exposure.  
• Panel data at the neighborhood/year level allow pre-vs-post comparisons and the inclusion of rich fixed effects.  
• The event-study version lets us test for parallel pre-trends and trace dynamics (credit tightening should fade after ≈3 years).

We will supplement DID with an IV (“Bartik”) robustness check that instruments the realized change in local HHI with the predicted change coming only from mergers of banks headquartered >250 miles away. This addresses potential endogenous within-market behavior (e.g., local acquisitions unrelated to the large mergers).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control Definition
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Level of observation: eight-digit lat/long “neighborhood cells” (≈ 0.1 mile radius), yearly 1990–2000.

Treatment variable(s):
TREAT_it  = 1{Post_t & Overlap_i,m}, where  

Overlap_i,m = 1 if neighborhood i had at least one branch of each of the two merging parents within 10 miles in the calendar year preceding merger m (the standard in the antitrust literature).  
Post_t = 1 for years ≥ the legal consummation year of merger m.  

Continuous version: ΔHHI_i,t = Σ_j (s_ij,t)^2 – Σ_j (s_ij,t-1)^2 , the change in neighborhood-level banking Herfindahl caused mechanically by the merger (shares s_ij fixed at the pre-merger branch distribution).

Control group:  

Neighborhoods in the same county that:  
(a) had at least one branch of only one of the two merging banks (“single-presence” controls); or  
(b) had branches of neither parent but at least one branch of some billion-$ bank (“other-presence” controls).  
These locations are subject to the same county-level macro shocks and data-collection quirks but do not experience the discrete rise in concentration.

Treatment timing / event date: year of legal consummation reported by the Fed’s merger approvals file (we verify using merger press releases). Event time k ∈ [-4,+6].

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends: Absent the merger, treated and control neighborhoods would have followed the same evolution in credit terms, construction, demographics, and crime.  
  Plausibility: Merging banks do not choose branch locations based on unobservable 1990s-era trends in crime or CRE prices; “single-presence” branches share similar markets, supporting common-trend plausibility. Pre-merger event-study coefficients will be shown.

A2. No simultaneous confounding shocks that differentially hit overlap neighborhoods exactly when the merger closes (e.g., local zoning changes).  
  Plausibility: Unlikely to coincide systematically with dozens of nationwide mergers, but we will control for county×year fixed effects and state-specific trends.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no cross-neighborhood spillovers within a county).  
  Plausibility: 10-mile credit market radius suggested by surveys; we drop “buffer” neighborhoods 10–20 miles away in robustness checks.

A4. Treatment exogeneity within event-time: merger completion is announced well in advance but consummation date is exogenous to local shocks.  
  Plausibility: Closing delays reflect Fed/DOJ review, not neighborhood-level conditions.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats and Mitigations
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Differential pre-trends / anticipation.  
  Mitigation: Include leads in the event-study; fail to reject zero for k ≤ -2; drop observations in announcement year to avoid anticipation.

T2. Endogenous local follow-on mergers or branch closings.  
  Mitigation: Keep banks other than the merging pair fixed in the calculation of ΔHHI; re-estimate after controlling for contemporaneous branch-density changes; IV version using only “remote” mergers.

T3. Spatial spillovers (credit constrained borrowers migrate).  
  Mitigation: Use crime and demographics measured at the same small geographies; when studying crime we include neighbor-cell outcomes to check for displacement.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
#--- 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # for fast TWFE and Sun & Abraham
library(lubridate)
library(Modelsummary)

#--- 1. Load data ------------------------------------------------------------
prop   <- fread("property_transactions.csv")      # COMPS data
merg   <- fread("fed_mergers.csv")                # merger file
branch <- fread("branch_locations_1990_2000.csv") # bank branches
crime  <- fread("capindex_cells.csv")             # CAP index data
census <- fread("census_tracts.csv")              # tract controls

#--- 2. Variable construction -----------------------------------------------
## 2.1 Assign each neighborhood cell to nearest branch per year
# Pre-compute distance-based market shares; here we pretend we have function calc_shares()
shares <- calc_shares(branch, radius = 10)  # returns cell_id, year, bank_id, share

## 2.2 Build ΔHHI attributable to each large merger
# Merge in merger parent IDs and closing year
shares <- merge(shares, merg[,.(bank_id=parent_id, merger_id, close_year)], by="bank_id", all.x=TRUE)

# For each cell and merger compute pre HHI and post HHI holding shares fixed => mechanical change
shares[, pre_HHI  := sum(share^2),                    by=.(cell_id, merger_id)]
shares[, post_HHI := pre_HHI - share[bank_in_merger==TRUE]^2 + (sum(share[bank_in_merger==TRUE]))^2,
       by=.(cell_id, merger_id)]
shares[, dHHI := post_HHI - pre_HHI]

## 2.3 Collapse to cell-year panel, keep largest dHHI in a given year (multiple mergers possible)
panel <- shares[, .(dHHI = max(dHHI)), by=.(cell_id, year)]
panel[, treat := as.numeric(dHHI>0)]

## 2.4 Merge outcomes
panel <- merge(panel, prop[,.(cell_id, year, int_rate, ltv, price_psf)], by=c("cell_id","year"), all.x=TRUE)
panel <- merge(panel, crime, by=c("cell_id","year"), all.x=TRUE)
panel <- merge(panel, census, by=c("tract_id","year"), all.x=TRUE)

#--- 3. Main TWFE specification ---------------------------------------------
# Outcome 1: interest rate on new CRE loans
reg1 <- feols(int_rate ~ treat                                # simple DiD
                     | cell_id + year,                        # two-way FE
              vcov = ~county_id, data = panel)

# Event-study using Sun & Abraham
panel[, rel_time := year - close_year]   # from merger file
reg_es <- feols(int_rate ~ sunab(rel_time, treat) | cell_id + year,
                vcov = ~county_id, data = panel[abs(rel_time)<=6])

#--- 4. Robustness: IV using remote mergers -------------------------------
# First stage: treat_hat = pi * Pred_dHHI
panel[, pred_dHHI := remote_merger_shift]  # pre-computed using only >250 mi mergers
iv1 <- feols(int_rate ~ 1 | cell_id + year | (dHHI ~ pred_dHHI),
             vcov = ~county_id, data = panel)

#--- 5. Output ---------------------------------------------------------------
modelsummary(list(DiD=reg1, EventStudy=reg_es, IV=iv1),
             stars = TRUE, output = "results_main.html")
```

Robustness checks to add: (i) drop buffer 10–20 mile cells; (ii) re-weight by cell CRE exposure; (iii) placebo using merger pairs that did not overlap in the study states.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Economic intuition: More concentrated credit markets → greater market power → higher interest rates and/or lower LTVs → reduced construction, lower property prices, falling in-migration of higher-income households → higher economic stress and potentially higher property crime.

Magnitude priors (per 1 SD ΔHHI ≈ 0.08):  
• CRE loan spreads: +35–50 bp (≈ ¼ SD of the sample distribution).  
• New construction value: −8 %.  
• Commercial property prices: −5 %.  
• Property crime CAP score: +0.15 SD; violent crime: +0.05 SD.  
Effects should peak 1–2 years post-merger and fade after 3 years.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Demonstrated parallel pre-trends in event study: 1  
C2: No spillovers or interference: 0.5 (some risk, partially mitigated)  
C3: Exogenous treatment timing relative to outcomes: 1  
C4: No differential compositional changes (e.g., property sample selection): 0.5  
C5: Robust standard errors/clustering and multiple robustness tests: 1  

Total ≈ 4/5 → credible but not bullet-proof.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
End of Plan
